correctness.rationale: Yamada's update is exactly \(R_i^{k+1}=R_i^k\cap(W\times\llbracket\varphi\rrbracket_{M^k})\). Therefore if a stage is strict, some surviving arrow into a currently false target \(v\) is removed, and the same target filter simultaneously removes every remaining incoming arrow to \(v\) for every source and agent. Thus \(v\) leaves the active-target set permanently, so every strict stage consumes at least one element of \(T_0\). The directed-cycle witness was reconstructed: initially only the unique \(p\)-false state fails the formula; deleting its incoming edge makes its predecessor a dead end, producing exactly one new false target each round until the last edge disappears at round \(n\).
risks: The sharp witness is a general modal frame and is not claimed sharp inside K45, KD45, or S5.
The theorem bounds update rounds, not the computational complexity of reevaluating the formula at each round.

evidence: Sharp \(|W|\) worst-case bound for all finite models.
value.rationale: This is a meaningful finite cutoff for the exact update process motivating the source's transfinite theory. It replaces a potentially huge labelled-arrow resource by a sharp linear state resource independent of the number of agents, and the matching family proves that no smaller universal state-only cutoff is possible on general frames.
risks: Additional epistemic frame axioms may allow stronger cutoffs.

final_claim: For any finite-state believed-public-announcement model and any fixed formula, iteration stabilizes after at most \(|T_0|\) strict updates, where \(T_0\) is the set of states initially targeted by some labelled arrow, hence after at most \(|W|\) strict updates; the bound is sharp for every \(n\ge1\) on an \(n\)-cycle with repeated announcement \(p\land\neg\Box\bot\).
limitations: Sharpness is only for general frames, not K45/KD45/S5 subclasses.
